lots.guide_summary: All of the guide is SOLD hammer prices at Gowans, Hobart, for generic mixed lots of 8 to 11 bottles: $50 to $95 (four lots, July to September 2026). Category guides: $34 to $52 for six unnamed whites, $190 for a six-bottle lot of unknown labels. The only named-bottle evidence is snippet-only retail (asking, not verified). No UNSOLD evidence. No Armitage past results found. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $50 (Gowans 429319, 9 mixed bottles incl. fortified) / 1.22 = $40.98, round down to $40. Flip: likely resale about $70 hammer (median of $50, $70, $85, $95), less 15% seller commission and no postage (sell locally by auction) = $59.50, / 2.44 = $24.39, round down to $20. Flip margin is negligible; this is a drinking lot.
lots.confidence_reason: Labels read clearly in the photos, but the SOLD comps are generic mixed lots, not these bottles, and storage and fill levels are unknown. Ageing whites (2010 to 2013) look deep gold in the photos, which may mean oxidation.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All Gowans ids re-checked in the API: titles, sale_price and bid counts match the researcher. Corrected the white-wine group aud_price from 45 to the lowest result (34). Wine-Searcher retail entry kept as a snippet-only lead.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows nine bottles. Photo 2: Patrick Piuze Chablis Terroir de Chichee, Vendanges 2012, and a 1977 German Spaetlese (Silvaner, eagle label). Photo 3: Monowai Pinot Noir, Shaw + Smith M3 Chardonnay Adelaide Hills 2013, Mildara Southern Cross Late Harvest Muscat Blanc. Photo 4: Lions Club 'Van Diemen's Tasmanian Devil Red Elixir' 1975 with foxed, stained label; Babich Black Label Sauvignon Blanc 2010; Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc (vintage not visible). The Chablis and M3 look deep gold or amber. Dogrock label is foxed. Fill levels cannot be judged from the photos.
lots.condition: Labels mostly clean. The novelty bottle and Dogrock labels are stained. Whites are 10 to 16 years old with deep colour, storage history unknown. Sauvignon Blancs (2010 Babich, Cloudy Bay) are likely past their best. The 1977 Spaetlese is a gamble.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you tell me the fill levels (especially the 1977 Spaetlese and the 1975 novelty bottle), the Cloudy Bay vintage, and whether the wines came from a cellar or were kept at room temperature? Are the Chablis and M3 as dark as they look in the photos?

lots.guide_summary: All same-item or close evidence is SOLD hammer at Gowans, Hobart: a near-identical white stepped skyscraper shade made $65 (June 2026); similar single deco skyscraper or beehive shades $50 to $80; a pair of deco skyscraper shades $120. All AUD, premium extra.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD for the key piece (deco skyscraper shade) = $50 (Gowans 427726) / 1.22 = $40.98, round down to $40. This values the skyscraper shade alone, so the other two come free. Flip: likely resale about $100 hammer for the three (skyscraper about $65 per 419677, cone and yellow globe about $15 to $20 each per the $16-a-shade pair 420653), less 15% seller commission, no postage (resold locally) = $85, / 2.44 = $34.84, round down to $30.
lots.confidence_reason: Unmarked glass, so there is no mark to read. One near-identical SOLD (419677) and several close SOLD skyscraper shades with photos checked, but condition (chips to fitter rims, cracks) cannot be confirmed from a single photo.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 13 Gowans ids re-checked in the API with matching titles, prices and bid counts. After checking the Gowans photos, 418059 (later swirl bowl), 420653 (flat painted shades), 432417 and 429172 (frilled tulip shades) and 370696 (type unknown) were moved from close to category guide. 419677 upgraded to same item. eBay and Etsy asking prices kept as snippet-only leads.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. White opal stepped octagonal skyscraper shade on a dull chrome fitter ring. Cream ribbed cone shade with a clear stepped glass top. Yellow custard-glass fluted globe with a plain lower band and collar. No marks visible, no obvious chips on the visible faces, but the fitter rims and the undersides are not shown.
lots.condition: Looks sound from one angle. Fitter rims, the inside and the collars are not shown. The chrome fitter is dull. Wiring and fittings unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any chips or cracks to the fitting rims or collars of the three shades, and does the chrome fitter on the stepped white shade come with a ceiling plate or wiring?
